xmldoc.short_description: Render the study report, carrying the research-only disclaimer.

param_input_item.param_description: an analysis from ecglab.analyze, or an ecglab.recording. A recording is analysed first (with ecglab.analyze when that function is present, and otherwise with the individual analysis functions), and the report is rendered from the analysis.

options as name and value pairs, matched without regard to case: File (a path the text is also written to; default '', none), Language ('en' by default, or 'fr' for French without accents), Width (the wrap column in characters; default 78).

param_output_item.param_description: the report as a char array with newlines. With no output argument the report is printed instead and nothing is returned; with an output argument the text is returned and nothing is printed.

description.p: The report is plain text, in sections, and its VERY FIRST lines are the research-only disclaimer: ecglab is research and teaching software, not a medical device. No number in the report is computed here; every value is read from the analysis structs, and a field the analysis left empty is printed as "not available" with a reason rather than a fabricated value.

Every interval is printed beside the AHA/ACC/HRS normal range, with a mark when it sits outside it. The mark is a MEASUREMENT flag, never a diagnosis: the report reports where a number sits, and never calls a measurement "abnormal" or reads it as a clinical finding.

The sections, in order: the subject, the source and the start of the recording when it is known; the length, the sampling rate and the leads; the signal quality (the usable fraction, and a line when a lead was refused); the heart rate (mean and range) and the rhythm (the dominant label, and the atrial fibrillation burden when any, printed as a measurement); the intervals PR, QRS, QT and the corrected QT by the four formulas (Bazett, Fridericia, Framingham, Hodges), each beside its normal range; the frontal axis with its label when the leads ran; the beats counted by the ANSI/AAMI class N, S, V, F, Q with their share; the heart rate variability summary (SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50, LF/HF) when it ran; and a provenance footer naming the detector, the Nelson build and the module version, and repeating once that this is research software.

With no output argument the report is printed and nothing is returned; with an output argument the text is returned and nothing is printed, so a caller can either read the report or capture it. The File option writes the same text to a file as well.

Research software, not a medical device. ecglab is for research and education. It is not a medical device and must not be used for clinical diagnosis, patient monitoring, treatment decisions, or any medical purpose.
